seo.description: Platform to learn for free and easily. An educational social network where students and teachers share knowledge.

meta.projectType: Create an application that facilitates interaction between students and teachers online, where the student can find all information in the desired format.
meta.description: Online educational platform for free courses

content.backgroundText: Thanks to the internet, many people have access to education despite not having the possibility of schooling. Platforms like YouTube, blogs, etc., help create learning. However, the difficulty of finding precise information for what we seek or a guide from start to finish on a general topic like architecture, mechanics, chemistry among many others, where reading, video, and images are needed, becomes difficult. The person searching gets blocked wasting a lot of time, piecing together information from different platforms. That is why Free Learn was born, all learning in a single social network.
content.allInOneText: That is what Free Learn aims to offer. A space for students to share their study guides, learning-related information, and where teachers can share diverse types of information: text, images, videos, live streams, polls, study groups, and a personalized learning filter. This benefits a very important industry like education, which is somewhat lagging in the present.
content.researchIntro: What is the point of exploring this solution? What user interactions are we talking about? Let's see how common user behaviors and patterns can help apply these design concepts.
content.goalsText: We interviewed 10 people with usability questions. Using the user empathy framework, we were able to understand their difficulties, the common flow for learning, and the flow for sharing information with their team.
content.resultText: People who use YouTube to learn also use Office Word to self-evaluate; people who learn online share their learning in WhatsApp groups.
content.userJourneyText: To empathize with users, we also created empathy maps and a user journey map to delve into each stage our personas go through when evaluating and finding the information they need.
content.userFlowText: We decided to invest our effort mainly in the most used user flow; we discovered it is finding information. Based on the discovery through the user flow, we could see how the views link together in this way.
content.architectureText: Designing the information architecture was easy to create because we knew the user flow. It was also accessible because from the beginning we thought of a hamburger menu or side menu.
content.crazyEightText: Taking the Information Architecture into account, we began organizing the corresponding elements in their views. We expanded our range of possibilities with the Crazy Eight exercise and finally refined based on user experience parameters (Accessibility, Simplicity, Intuitive, and Inclusivity).
content.wireframesText: Having the wireframes ready on paper, we started digitizing them, giving each element a coordinate on the screen according to its hierarchy and weight, so the user can be guided step by step through the design to complete the main goal.
content.lowFidelityText: Once digital wireframes were created, we started prototyping. This helped us know if our internal linking logic worked well, create more accesses to the same place, and discard what didn't work.
content.usabilityTestingIntro: We wanted to know how the user navigates between views, how long it takes to access information, and see their reactions when executing a task. All this was done during the Testing Plan process. The participants chosen were 6 people of different ages, professions, and skills.
content.usabilityTestingResult: During the interview, we learned that the questions the user couldn't answer might contain information mentioned on the card to be more accessible and consequently save more interaction time. We interpreted the Wireframe and resolved the notice.
backgroundExperienceQuestions: Could you briefly introduce yourself and tell me about your experience with technology and mobile applications?
How often do you use online course apps and social networks?
Have you previously used applications that combine both functionalities?
appExperienceQuestions: Could you briefly introduce yourself and tell me about your experience with the application?
Could you describe your general experience using the app so far?
What aspects of the application have you found easiest to use?
Have you encountered any difficulties or problems using the application? If so, could you describe them in detail?
How would you rate the general ease of use of the app on a scale of 1 to 5 (1 being very difficult and 5 being very easy)?
Have you used the application to search for and take online courses?
Could you describe the process of searching for a specific course? Was it easy to find what you were looking for?
How would you rate the ease of use of the online courses section on a scale of 1 to 5?
Have you completed any lesson or activity within a course? Could you describe your experience in that process?
How would you rate the ease of use of the lessons and activities section on a scale of 1 to 5?
Have you interacted with a teacher or classmate in any course? Could you describe your experience in that case?
What aspects of the online courses section could be improved?
content.mockupsText: Once the Wireframes were refined, we dedicated ourselves to laying out all the elements adding colors, weights, shadows, typography, etc.
content.designSystemText: The combination of blue and turquoise under a black background to give contrast to something new and futuristic, the Roboto typography to give an elegant and technological tone, the sizes in buttons and the contrast in them so that people with color vision deficiency can differentiate it easily.
content.conclusionText: The product is Free Learn, a social network for everyone to learn easily and for free. We are still working on the views and components to show the final product.

seo.description: I implemented with a colleague a design refactoring of a real estate landing page in Cancún.

meta.projectType: Landing page for a real estate agency in Cancún
meta.description: I implemented with a colleague a design refactoring of a real estate landing page.

sections.ctaDescription: Explore more of my work and discover how I can help you create exceptional digital experiences.

content.backgroundText: The idea arose from the need to improve the user experience on the website of a real estate agency in Cancún. Here we implemented the branding of a more luxurious, intuitive, and professional page. We improved the main filter so that it redirects to more specific properties from there.
content.researchText: User research, we obtained data from people who visit, those who buy properties, those who search for properties, and those who rent properties. Thanks to Google Analytics we were able to identify the people who interact most with the page and those who spend the most time on the page; the page conversion rate was 10% and the interaction time was 2 minutes.
content.resultText: We found that users tend to look for the most exclusive and secure properties. We also found that users who buy properties are people who have large families and want security in their investment such as proximity to the beach.
painPointsList: People feel their investment is risky if there is no security in the properties
They need a platform that helps them find secure properties
They want to know the property through images and videos
It is difficult to contact agencies
content.architectureText: A landing page architecture was planned with a main filter that redirects to more specific properties.

seo.description: App for every citizen to present their dissatisfaction regarding a public service in Benito Juárez.

meta.projectType: Citizen reporting platform, public services, mismanagement
meta.description: Citizen Report Benito Juárez is an App for every citizen to present their dissatisfaction regarding a public service. The platform facilitates the process of reporting problems related to municipal services, infrastructure, and public administration.

sections.ctaDescription: Explore more of my work and discover how I can help you create exceptional digital experiences.

content.backgroundText: Citizen Report Benito Juárez is an App for every citizen to present their dissatisfaction regarding a public service.
content.researchGoals: 15 people were interviewed and asked the questions presented in the image, to know if they had made any report and what the process to do so is.
content.researchResult: Few people have made a report; to make their dissatisfaction known they comment among citizens but never to the corresponding authority, also they do not know who to turn to.
content.userJourneyText: After understanding user needs, we created themes to be able to extract design ideas that later managed to respond punctually to user needs.
content.userFlowText: We decided to recreate the entire process a user goes through to make a report, as well as extracting ideas on how we would punctually solve those processes.
content.architectureText: Once all processes and themes were taken into account, we generated the design architecture to organize what information goes in each view and how they will connect with each other.
content.crazyEightsText: Finally, to have a guiding sketch of where to direct our effort regarding interface design, we did the famous Crazy Eight exercise that explores design ideas our interface can take and takes the best of each one to finally have a final design.
content.wireframesText: We improved spaces, shapes, and content by digitizing the wireframes.
content.lowFidelityText: We visibly clarified links and internal actions within the design to then iterate internally in the team and corrected some internal connections.
content.usabilityTestingText: To finish the first stage, we wanted to survey users about the platform and obtain feedback such as observing how easy or difficult it was for users to navigate. During the interview, we learned that it was actually easy and intuitive for the user; however, some elements like text needed context despite already having an idea of what they were for. We iterated on the Wireframes and resolved the notice. Key Performance Indicator Questions: These are quantifiable measures used to evaluate the success of an organization, project, or activity based on its objectives.

usability: How easy was it for you to understand the purpose of the citizen reporting platform?
How intuitive was the navigation on the platform?
Did you encounter any technical problems while using the platform?
design: Did you like the general design of the platform?
Were the user interface elements clearly labeled?
Was the workflow on the platform logical and consistent?
functional: Did the functions available on the platform meet your expectations?
Do you consider that the citizen reporting platform would be useful for solving community problems?
How likely are you to recommend this platform to other people?

content.mockupsText: Once the Wireframes were refined, we dedicated ourselves to laying out all the elements adding colors, weights, shadows, typography, etc.
content.conclusionText: Citizen Report Benito Juárez is an App for every citizen to present their dissatisfaction regarding a public service.

yiapp.title: YiApp e-commerce of clothing and accessories

seo.description: Yi is a multi-brand, multi-payment, multi-shipping address, multi-packaging apparel retail app.

meta.projectType: Mobile App - This design is a multi-brand and multi-delivery online clothing store application for the general public.
meta.description: YiApp is a mobile e-commerce application specialized in clothing and accessories. The platform offers an intuitive and secure shopping experience, allowing users to explore a wide variety of products, make quick purchases, and manage their orders efficiently. With an attractive design and advanced functionalities, YiApp positions itself as an ideal option for fashion lovers looking for convenience and style in one place.

content.researchIntro: What's the point of exploring this solution? Which user's interactions are involved? Let's see how common user behaviors and patterns can help to enforce these design concepts.
content.goalsText: To understand the user's needs we conducted a user interview to identify their normal flow in an application, find out what problem they would like to solve and understand how an enhanced wearable application can help. With the research we tried to identify areas of opportunity to create in our application.
content.resultText: Thanks to that research we were able to identify the common path of a user to achieve their purchase objective. With the field research we were able to identify the areas of opportunity and from the result we came up with themes such as Multiple Addresses, Multiple Payment Methods and found that the whole multi-click checkout process could be simplified into a single view.
content.userJourneyText: To empathize with users, we also create empathy maps and a user journey map to delve into each stage our personas go through when buying a product.
content.userFlowText: To understand how we would build the experience we designed the main user flows for the Yi application, The user flow allowed us to see the whole application experience on a holistic level and thus make decisions
content.architectureBrainstorm: Once we had gathered the topics and identified the user flows, it was time to start creating an architecture map of how the information would be organized in the design, we brainstormed ideas, separating what did not meet the objectives and saving it for future ideas.
content.architectureComplete: After the brainstorming we could clearly complete the information architecture by organizing each view according to its data, this also allows us to scale the application in the future and divide it into components making it easier to iterate and improve if required.
content.crazyEightText: Once we had all the information ready and organized we started to create our mockups based on an exercise called "Crazy Eight" this helped us to extend the panorama of identifying different ways of views and based on that to choose a final design gathering elements from the other views evaluating simplicity, accessibility, inclusiveness and finally the design.
content.wireframesText: Iterating on the paper wireframes we started to create the digital wireframes, this helped us to identify real spaces within a device, it also clarified our ideas of where the final design was going, at this stage I learned that the elements must be understandable for all people and not just for me, so every thing that people didn't understand had a label.
content.lowFidelityText: After confirming our scenarios we started to put together some fundamentals of Yi, we wanted the user to choose their product and buy it, as if each step was a small part of the whole thing. The low fidelity wireframes helped us rule out some features that were not as fundamental as the shopping cart search.
content.usabilityTestingIntro: We ran several participants through our low-fidelity prototype to better understand their patterns of interaction patterns. Each of them was given the simple task to buy a product. It wasn't the difficult task, but it was how they thought through the process of buying a product we were interested in.
usabilityQuestions: ❓ Did you find it easy or difficult to buy a product? If your answer is very difficult or moderately difficult, what made it difficult for you
❓ If you could change anything about the process, what would you change?
❓ Did you find it easy or difficult to add the product to your wish list?
❓ I find it easy to navigate the application. KPI
❓ There are inconsistencies within the app. KPI
❓ I would imagine that most people would learn to use this app quickly. KPI
❓ I think I would use this app frequently. KPI
content.usabilityResult: During the survey we learned that the user expected a deeper accessibility that translates into easy navigation and thanks to that we came up with themes and then the following solutions until we have solved the problem.
content.mockupsText: After solidifying the foundational framework, we were able to take the feedback from our testing sessions and start to form our final comps. We used color sparingly throughout the product to help communicate interactable elements to the user and guide it sequentially to the main objective.
content.designSystemText1: The green color was selected to show creativity and innovation on each product that is sold, the semicircular corners represent fun but confidence by not being so circular.
content.designSystemText2: The brand logo is a creation of two names Yohana Isaac, the bag in the cart is the identity of the brand as objectively the purchases in the application can be organized by bags and then add to cart but you can also add the products individually.
content.conclusionText: Yi is a multi-brand, multi-payment, multi-shipping address, multi-packaging apparel retail app.

propiedadesCancun.description: I optimized the performance, SEO architecture, and user experience of a real estate portal, achieving a 25% increase in organic traffic and ranking property pages on the first page of Google.

header.title: How I increased organic traffic by 25% by optimizing the architecture of Propiedades Cancún
header.subtitle: Real estate portal · Role: Frontend Developer · Development team

caseStudy.summary: I optimized the performance, SEO architecture, and user experience of a real estate portal, achieving a 25% increase in organic traffic and ranking property pages on the first page of Google.

results.label: Google ranking positions for the main transactional pages (first page)
Users staying past 3 seconds on the site

items: I refactored the visual components applying Gestalt and contrast principles to direct attention toward the call-to-action buttons.
I simplified the interface so every element had a clear purpose. Users staying past 3 seconds went from 25% to 65%, and those reaching the one-minute mark increased by 50%.
I automated image conversion to WebP format and adjusted their quality, reducing their weight by 40% with no visible loss.
I inlined critical CSS to render visible content first and reduce LCP.
I improved the Lighthouse SEO score up to 100%.
I measured HTTP response times with Screaming Frog to validate the improvements.
I designed semantic URLs based on search intent, avoiding keyword cannibalization between dynamic pages.
I automated the generation of unique titles and meta descriptions for each property, making indexing easier at scale.
I optimized robots.txt to reduce the crawl budget and set up 301 redirects to preserve the domain's authority.

I developed an algorithm that prioritizes the most relevant properties by combining the ranking assigned by the administrator with the most frequent searches in Google Analytics and Search Console within a short time window, with no additional server load.
I set up GitHub Actions pipelines that run tests with Vitest, validate the build, and deploy automatically on every change, keeping errors out of production and speeding up delivery.

The system had to be ready before the semester closed and support 300 students uploading simultaneously.

results.label: System delivered before the semester closed
Students across 4 programs using the system

items: I designed and optimized SQL queries and database relationships to support simultaneous file uploads during the semester close.
I structured the business logic into reusable services using Laravel's service container and object-oriented programming.
I validated file type, size, and format with Form Requests before storing them.
I used Laravel collections to filter and group information by group, program, and status.
I standardized backend responses using API resources.
I implemented JWT authentication and middleware to protect the routes.
I set up role-based access control (RBAC) with Laravel policies, so each student could only access their own documents while administrators managed their area through the same endpoints.
I built the document upload forms for students.
I built the collection lists CRUD, with advanced sorting and filtering by group and program.
I implemented the per-document status flow (pending, under review, approved, rejected) with admin feedback to the student.
I built reminders so students would upload their documents on time, sent by email with scheduled notifications.
I wrote unit tests with PHPUnit and behavior specs with PhpSpec.
I applied Clean Code principles so the system would stay maintainable for future semesters.

caseStudy.summary: I independently built, from design to deployment, the platform for an artisanal flower arrangement business: a public catalog optimized for SEO, an admin panel so the client can manage her products without depending on a developer, and the API connecting both.

results.label: Products managed directly by the client, in production
Technical interventions needed for the client to update the catalog
From design to production deployment, solo

items: I defined the product scope with the client to prioritize what was needed for the first version.
I prototyped the interface with Claude Design to iterate quickly and polished the visual details in Figma.
I validated the flows and expected states in Figma before building them, to avoid rework.
I designed the project's architecture, separating the public catalog, the admin panel, and the API.
I built RESTful APIs with NestJS, following its modular structure of controllers, services, and DTOs, along with data validation.
I modeled the database in MongoDB with collections for products, categories, and admin users, plus indexes by category to speed up catalog filtering.
I implemented a Backend for Frontend (BFF) in Next.js to centralize API calls and avoid exposing the API directly to the browser.
I tested the endpoints with Postman and wrote unit and integration tests with Jest.
I built the catalog with Next.js and SSR so every product is indexed correctly on Google.
I implemented category filters to browse the catalog without reloading the page.
I integrated a WhatsApp contact button that sends a message with the product's name and price, making it easier to request a quote.
I configured SEO metadata and Open Graph tags to improve ranking and the preview when shared on social media.
I optimized images in WebP format and served them from a media subdomain via Cloudflare to reduce load times.
I built a responsive interface, designed mainly for mobile, since customers arrive mostly through social media.
